_comment:
The example instance's own declaration -- the same file `instance/config.json` is for the instance that happens to run this repository, written for one that does not exist. `owner: instance` below is what it would say once copied into place, and copying it into place is exactly what `tools/tests/repository/test_second_instance.py` does before building: the second instance is not a set of overrides applied to this one, it is a repository with these files where the boundary says the instance's files go.

Manifestly synthetic, and every field is checkable as such. The forum, the contact address and the proposal form are all under `.test`, which RFC 2606 reserves and no registry will ever delegate. The organisation, the series, the people and the institutions in `../data/speakers.yml` do not exist.

The one address that cannot be under a reserved name is `published_url`: `Published.publish_repository` derives the repository the built site is pushed into from it, and it derives it only from a GitHub Pages project address (`https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/`). An `example.test` address there would make this instance refuse a derivation the real one performs, which would leave the most load-bearing half of the declaration untested by the very build that exists to test it. `example-instance` is not a name anybody is asked to register and nothing here resolves it; that it is a shape GitHub could in principle host is the price of exercising the derivation.
_edition_prefix_comment:
The prefix this instance numbers its editions under, and the point of the key being its own. `MRG` is the Monthly Reading Group's, and it is deliberately neither `identity.short_name` (`TEC`) nor anything the product chooses: the two have no reason to move together, and `short_name` is prose, which gets reworded, while an edition code cannot be.

`../data/speakers.yml` numbers its sessions `MRG-1`, `MRG-2`, `MRG-3` from this one value, `validate.validate_speakers` builds its pattern from it, and `tools/tests/repository/test_second_instance.py` builds this whole repository from this declaration and refuses anything of the other instance's numbering in what comes out.
_charter_comment: The design this instance is drawn in, named rather than written. `assets/brand/convener/` is the product's own charter, and naming it is the whole of what the `charter` key buys: the file stays where upstream maintains it, so a contrast remeasured or a token renamed there reaches a duplicate as an ordinary merge instead of as a conflict on a file it now owns.\n\nWhat this example gives up by naming one, because it is a real loss rather than a free choice: it no longer carries a charter of its own, so it no longer shows a reader that an instance can. It carried one -- a dark green and an ochre -- and the three screenshots `README.md` shows were rendered from it, so the front page of the product showed one design while the mark at the top of that same page showed another. Those screenshots render this instance and can render no other: `tools/visuals/render-readme-shots.mjs` refuses to run in a repository that has been configured, for the reason its own comment gives. The shop window and the mark agree only if this declaration names the mark's own charter. What stops being demonstrated here is still stated and still held: `publication/brand.py::source` gives the three answers an instance may make about its design -- it writes one, it names one of the product's, or it makes neither answer -- and refuses the fourth, and `tools/tests/publication/test_brand.py` builds a repository for each of them.

identity.tagline: An invented series, shipped as this product's own worked example.
